sampling_model.design: Two randomized regime studies report complete \(2\times2\) tables, one under \(\operatorname{do}(Z=0)\) and one under \(\operatorname{do}(X=0)\).
sampling_model.units: The population version treats \(A\) and \(B\) as exact laws of one SCM; the optional sampling result uses multinomial frequency tables of sizes \(nA\) and \(nB\).
sampling_model.treatment: The first regime fixes \(Z=0\) and leaves \(X\) natural; the second fixes \(X=0\) and leaves \(Z\) natural.
sampling_model.overlap: Strict positivity of all eight population cells implies \(0<p,r<1\), \(0<a<p\), and \(0<b<r\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance functions are estimated. The optional interval uses only empirical multinomial cells and simultaneous concentration.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: When the generic finite discrete-SCM polynomial program is instantiated with the present product-disturbance graph, two experimental inputs, and target, its minimization and maximization give sharp lower and upper bounds.
Counterfactual consistency of overlapping categorical marginal SCMs restricts the admissible marginal and joint SCMs.
Every categorical SCM has a finite canonical SCM with the same graph and all the same counterfactual distributions.
EMCC returns fully specified compatible SCMs whose counterfactual range approximates the actual bounds from inside.
The global extrema of a response-function linear program occur at vertices of its feasible polytope.

body.tldr: Two complete experiments on overlapping margins of a binary collider need not arise from one SCM. For arbitrary normalized binary tables, including structural-zero faces, the note proves an iff compatibility inequality and a closed-form sharp interval for the all-zero joint-intervention risk. A single finite ordered-threshold construction preserves the two independent source roots, uses one deterministic outcome law in every regime, and attains every feasible value with at most eight private-noise atoms. The result yields constant-time endpoints, exact rational endpoint certificates, and an optional conservative sampling interval for this fixed graph.

project_justification.gap: General discrete-SCM methods can optimize this query numerically, and causal-marginal methods explain why overlapping reports must be consistent, but neither checked line supplies the graph-specific compatibility frontier, analytic endpoints, or a small common-SCM witness.
project_justification.niche: The fixed binary collider collapses to four natural-treatment strata, yet source independence prevents the armwise completions and unrestricted latent couplings used in simpler partial-identification arguments.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the two-mass fiber on the closed probability simplex, proves a source-preserving finite extension with explicit zero-denominator branches, and packages the resulting iff test and max--min interval as an exact analytic certificate for the same fixed input that Autobounds handles through generic polynomial optimization.

body.related_work: Gresele et al. formulate the structural causal marginal problem and show how one shared response-function law constrains overlapping causal models; their main analytic Boolean construction is causally sufficient, while their confounded extension retains a high-dimensional partially factorized law. Duarte et al. prove that sharp discrete causal bounds under observational and experimental evidence reduce to polynomial programs and implement the generic method in Autobounds. The present closed-simplex model, intervention menu, and target form a binary product-disturbance specialization within that scope, so the generic sharpness theorem applies to the corresponding optimization problem; it does not provide the graph-specific compatibility inequality, closed-form endpoints, or at-most-eight-atom common-SCM certificates derived here. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim prove finite canonical SCM sufficiency for arbitrary categorical counterfactual distributions; the present threshold lift is a smaller menu-specific certificate, not a generic canonicalization theorem. Sachs, Jonzon, Sjoelander, and Gabriel derive tight symbolic bounds for response-function models with linear constraints; their elimination logic is adjacent, while the independent latent-source structure here is preserved explicitly. Zaffalon et al. fuse heterogeneous observational and randomized studies through causal EM and report approximate inner ranges, making their work adjacent multi-source bounding rather than the exact analytic result proved here. Shridharan and Iyengar reduce the degree of multilinear causal-bound programs in quasi-Markovian graphs, while Finkelstein and Shpitser and Balke and Pearl supply related inequality and response-type templates; none of these checked results states the present closed-simplex formulas.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The source-preserving extension is proved on the entire closed simplex by explicit zero-mass branches; it does not rely on continuity from positive tables. Independence of the two source roots remains load-bearing: allowing them to be correlated can move the target outside the independent-source interval. The at-most-eight-atom construction is an upper certificate, not an optimal-support theorem, and the optional sampling interval is conservative rather than tie-optimal.
body.honest_scope: The result covers arbitrary normalized binary tables, including structural zeros, for exactly the collider graph, the two stated experimental regimes, mutually independent shared roots, private outcome noise, and the all-zero joint-intervention risk. Correlated or dependence-budget source roots, different study populations, a simultaneous region for all four joint-intervention risks, three or more parents, minimal support, nominal tie-robust inference, general thicket compilation, and any field-tier claim remain excluded. Any assertion of a strictly positive identified-set width is explicitly confined to the interior regime \(0<p,r<1\); no positive-width assertion is made on support faces. If regime \(B\) is omitted, the mass accounting gives \(q\in[a,a+1-p]\); symmetrically, omitting regime \(A\) gives \(q\in[b,b+1-r]\).
